- name: Heterogeneous Echogenicity on Ultrasound
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: heterogeneous echogenicity with rich vascularity and ill-defined margins
  description: >-
    Ultrasound is the modality of choice for small, superficial lesions. KHE is heterogeneous in
    echogenicity, with striated hypoechoic bands in some, and usually richly vascular (abundant or
    patchy flow in the 2023 series), though its overall echogenicity varies: in a 2023 series of 27
    infants, the masses seen were moderately echoic in 13, hypoechoic in 9 and hyperechoic in 4 (one
    infant had no mass on ultrasound), and in a 2019 comparison of 40 KHE and 21 tufted angiomas,
    KHE was more likely than tufted angioma to be hypoechoic. In that comparison, 96.15% of KHE (no
    denominator given) had mixed echogenicity, against hyperechoic lesions in 42.9% of tufted
    angiomas, every KHE had ill-defined margins, and 3-D colour Doppler showed branch-shaped flow.
    In a 2018 series, in which 15 children had ultrasound, the masses were inhomogeneous and rich in
    vascularity. Ultrasound alone may not separate KHE from infantile haemangioma, as both look
    hypervascular; a 2023 comparison table lists heterogeneous echogenicity, ill-defined margins and
    an infiltrative pattern for KHE against an echogenic, well-defined mass for rapidly involuting
    congenital haemangioma.
  notes: >-
    Left without a bound term. Of the 81 hits of runoak -i sqlite:obo:ncit search "l~echo", eight
    lie in the NCIT imaging-finding branch: Echo Pattern (NCIT:C208177), a generic parent defined as
    the composition of ultrasound waves, its children Anechoic, Isoechoic, Hyperechoic and
    Hypoechoic, and Hypoechoic Focus, Hyperechoic Focus and Hyperechoic Strand. The children and the
    focus terms each name a single pattern or feature, and none names the mixed and varying
    echogenicity the sources report. Heterogeneous Echotexture (NCIT:C69214) sits under Image
    Feature, outside the branch.

- name: Bone Destruction or Remodelling
  modality: MRI
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: destruction or remodelling of bone
    term:
      id: HP:0002797
      label: Osteolysis
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: bone destruction
    term:
      id: HP:0002797
      label: Osteolysis
  description: >-
    The 2020 review calls bone and joint changes next to the tumour common: destruction of the
    adjacent cortex, injury of the epiphyseal region and invasion of nearby joints. Destructive
    changes or remodelling of adjacent bone were among the most common presenting features in a
    64-patient MRI series, in 42.2%, more often from 6 months of age, and MRI showed bone
    destruction in 24 (34%) of a 70-patient series (how many had MRI is not stated), the ribs most
    often. In other series: bone changes in 4 patients of a 12-patient series (10 had CT or MRI
    findings), whose authors call them infrequent; reported with the CT findings of a 2018 series
    (13 with CT), ill-defined osteolytic destruction in one patient and erosion or remodelling of
    adjacent bone in three; and in a 2023 series, bone invasion in 3 of the 12 with CT and bone
    changes in 1 of the 4 with MRI. The 2018 authors call CT useful for showing osteolytic
    destruction, erosion and remodelling, and the 2023 authors, citing them, say CT shows these
    better. In a separate series of 12 children whose KHE was confined to bone on first imaging,
    two patterns appeared: a permeative or moth-eaten osteolytic pattern in 7, which the authors
    describe as involving epiphysis and metaphysis, one of the 7 with both patterns; and
    well-defined, saucer-like cortical excavation in 5, mainly of the metaphysis (4 of 5; one
    epiphyseal); none of the 12 had a significant periosteal reaction.
  notes: >-
    Osteolysis (HP:0002797) covers the destructive changes, not remodelling. Of the 9 hits of
    runoak -i sqlite:obo:ncit search "l~osteoly", the two in the NCIT imaging-finding branch are
    osteolytic lesions of multiple myeloma and of metastasis, while Osteolysis (NCIT:C50681) and
    Osteolytic (NCIT:C14149) are outside it; "l~bone destr" has no hits, and none of the 427 hits of
    "l~erosi" or the 13 of "l~remodel" is in the branch. The row's modality follows the 64-patient
    MRI series; the 12-patient, 2018 and 2023 series and the series of KHE confined to bone used CT
    or MRI, and the 2018 authors call CT useful for bone destruction while the 2023 authors, citing
    them, say it shows it better. The series of KHE confined to bone is of tumours arising in bone,
    not bone next to a soft-tissue tumour.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.

    explanation: >-

  modality: CT

  description: >-
    On unenhanced CT, KHE is isodense with muscle: isoattenuating in the 13 with CT in a 2018 series
    of 25, and heterogeneous and isodense, about 30 HU on average, in a 2023 series of 27 infants

    enhancement, in 10 of the 11 with contrast CT in the 2023 series.
  notes: >-
    Bound to Isointense (NCIT:C28044), which NCIT defines as areas with the same intensity as other
    objects on imaging scans, not for one modality nor relative to muscle; runoak -i sqlite:obo:ncit
    search "l~isoatt" and "l~isoden" return no hits. The binding covers the unenhanced finding; the
    arterial-phase enhancement is given in the description and evidence.

- name: Diffusion on Diffusion-Weighted MRI
  modality: MRI
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging
  description: >-
    The two series that report diffusion-weighted imaging differ. In the 2018 series, the 5 masses
    imaged showed slightly restricted diffusion, with a mean apparent diffusion coefficient of 1.28
    × 10⁻³ mm²/s; its authors say a low apparent diffusion coefficient helps distinguish KHE from
    infantile haemangioma (the series imaged no haemangiomas), and that the value of diffusion
    imaging in diagnosis needs testing in larger cohorts. In the 2023 series, the KHE imaged by MRI
    (4 of 27 infants; how many had diffusion imaging is not stated) showed no significant diffusion
    restriction.
  notes: >-
    Left without a bound term. Of the 525 hits of runoak -i sqlite:obo:ncit search "l~diffus", four
    lie in the NCIT imaging-finding branch: Diffusion Restriction (NCIT:C182357), which asserts
    restricted diffusion while the two series disagree on whether diffusion is restricted;
    Non-Gaussian Water Diffusion Pattern; and two diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma morphology
    findings.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29536769
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical and imaging features of Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

      lymphedema.
    explanation: >-
      The 2018 series: KHE showed slightly restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging.

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

histopathology:
- name: Infiltrating Vascular Nodules
  description: >-
    The histological hallmark in the review: infiltrating, defined, rounded and confluent nodules of
    spindle endothelial cells. The 33-case series describes irregular, infiltrating nodules of
    compressed vessels that in places resemble a capillary haemangioma and in others Kaposi sarcoma;
    in three adult cases densely packed spindle cells grew in a lobular or nodular pattern, closely
    associated with small slit-like and sieve-like vessels; and in most of eight cases nodular
    growth predominated over a minor spindle-cell component, with the nodules of tumours in the
    extremities infiltrating dermis and subcutaneous fat. In a thoracic series of 7 KHE and 6
    kaposiform lymphangiomatosis patients, the nodules of KHE were more defined and confluent than
    the sparse, poorly marginated spindle-cell clusters of kaposiform lymphangiomatosis.
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: infiltrating nodules of spindle endothelial cells and compressed vessels
    term:
      id: NCIT:C35900
      label: Multinodular Pattern
  diagnostic: true
  notes: >-
    Bound to Multinodular Pattern, defined as cells forming multiple nodules within a lesion, since
    the nodules are the review's hallmark and every source describes several; Infiltrative Growth
    Pattern (NCIT:C41453) names only their infiltration. An NCIT label search for "Nodul" returned
    243 terms, 12 of them in the histopathology branch, none combining nodules with infiltration or
    with spindle endothelial cells (27 Nov 2026).
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The histologic hallmark of KHE is infiltrating, defined, rounded and confluent nodules, which
      are composed of spindle endothelial cells.
    explanation: >-
      The review names the hallmark: infiltrating, rounded, confluent nodules of spindle endothelial
      cells.
  - reference: PMID:15105642
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a study of 33 cases emphasizing its pathologic,
      immunophenotypic, and biologic uniqueness from juvenile hemangioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Tumors consisted of irregular, infiltrating nodules of compressed vessels, which modulated
      between areas resembling a capillary hemangioma and Kaposi sarcoma (KS).
    explanation: >-
      In the 33-case series, irregular infiltrating nodules of compressed vessels, modulating
      between capillary-haemangioma-like and Kaposi-sarcoma-like areas.
  - reference: PMID:9322599
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma in adults. Clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical analysis
      of three cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT

    snippet: >-
      Histologically, in all cases a lobular or nodular growth pattern of densely packed
      spindle-shaped tumor cells closely associated with small slitlike and sievelike blood vessels
      was seen.
    explanation: >-
      In three adult cases, a lobular or nodular pattern of densely packed spindle cells with
      slit-like and sieve-like vessels.
  - reference: PMID:33722245
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma: clinicopathological characteristics of 8 cases of a rare
      vascular tumor and review of literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Most cases showed predominance of nodular growth and a minor component of spindle cell
      population along with lymphangiomatosis like vascular channels, with evidence of microthrombi
      in 2 cases.
    explanation: >-
      In most of eight cases, predominantly nodular growth with a minor spindle-cell component;
      lymphangioma-like vessels in 4 of 8 (the paper's Table 2) and microthrombi in 2.
  - reference: PMID:33722245
    reference_title: >-

  - reference: PMID:31277673
    reference_title: >-

      differences.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In KLA, the spindle cells were distributed in sparse and poorly marginated clusters, whereas

- name: Glomeruloid Islands with Pericytes and Fibrin Thrombi
  description: >-
    Scattered "epithelioid" or glomeruloid islands of endothelium with clusters of plump
    actin-positive pericytes, stippled haemosiderin and CD61-positive fibrin thrombi, which the
    33-case series takes to be the likely sites where platelets are consumed; the eight-case series'
    introduction describes the nodules as glomeruloid aggregates of vascular channels with a
    surrounding pericytic layer. The abstract on three adult cases describes small nodules of
    plumper, epithelioid tumour cells in one lesion, and well-formed capillaries frequently
    containing fibrin thrombi mainly at the periphery of the nodules, without calling either
    glomeruloid.
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: glomeruloid islands with pericytes, haemosiderin and fibrin thrombi
    term:
      id: NCIT:C35926
      label: Glomeruloid Vessels Present
  notes: >-
    Glomeruloid Vessels Present names the islands (an NCIT label search for "Glomeruloid" returned
    it and Glomeruloid Hemangioma, 27 Nov 2026); the pericytes, haemosiderin and fibrin thrombi are
    carried in the description.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:15105642
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a study of 33 cases emphasizing its pathologic,
      immunophenotypic, and biologic uniqueness from juvenile hemangioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Scattered "epithelioid" or glomeruloid islands featuring endothelium associated with clusters
      of plump alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive pericytes, stippled hemosiderin, and CD61-positive
      fibrin thrombi likely represent the morphologic sites of platelet consumption.
    explanation: >-
      Glomeruloid islands with actin-positive pericytes, haemosiderin and CD61-positive fibrin
      thrombi, which the authors take to be the likely sites of platelet consumption.
  - reference: PMID:33722245
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma: clinicopathological characteristics of 8 cases of a rare
      vascular tumor and review of literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The nodules are glomeruloid aggregates of vascular channels, with variable slit-like lumina
      and surrounding pericytic layer.
    explanation: >-
      The eight-case series' introduction: the nodules are glomeruloid aggregates of vascular
      channels with a pericytic layer.
  - reference: PMID:9322599
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma in adults. Clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical analysis
      of three cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Well-formed capillaries frequently containing fibrin thrombi were observed mainly in the
      periphery of tumor nodules.
    explanation: >-
      The abstract on three adult cases reports well-formed capillaries frequently containing fibrin
      thrombi, mainly at the periphery of the nodules. INDIRECT: it does not call them glomeruloid.
  - reference: PMID:9322599
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma in adults. Clinicopathologic and immunohistochemical analysis
      of three cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Within one lesion, small nodules of plumper, epithelioid tumor cells were identified.
    explanation: >-
      Small nodules of plumper, epithelioid cells in one adult lesion, the nearest counterpart in
      that abstract to the 33-case series' epithelioid islands. INDIRECT: not called glomeruloid
      there, and the abstract does not place pericytes, haemosiderin or thrombi in these nodules.
- name: Lymphatic Channels Within and Around the Tumour
  description: >-
    Lymphatic channels are found within and around the tumour. The review describes the spindle
    cells as aligning into malformed lymphatic channels; the 33-case series found small and large
    lymphatic channels in 22 of 33 cases, typically at the periphery of or deep to the main mass;
    and in the eight-case series lymphangioma-like vessels were recorded in 4 of 8 tumours (its
    Table 2), and one case had prominent lymphatic vessels around the nodules. One of three adult
    cases had an associated lymphangiomatosis of the dermis and subcutis.
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: intralesional and peritumoural lymphatic channels
    term:
      id: NCIT:C35976
      label: Vascular Channel Formation
  notes: >-
    Bound to Vascular Channel Formation, its vascular passages read to include lymphatic ones, as
    NCIT itself files Cavernous Lymphatic Space Formation under Cavernous Vascular Space Formation;
    its "newly formed" fits the channels the spindle cells form within the nodules, while the
    sources do not say whether the peritumoural channels are new. NCIT label searches for "Lymphatic
    Channel" returned nothing; for "Lymphatic Vess", anatomy, neoplasm, tissue and receptor-protein
    terms outside the histopathology branch; for "Lymphang", 36 terms, none in the branch; and for
    "Lymphatic", 77 terms, two in the branch: Lymphatic Invasion (NCIT:C47850) and Cavernous
    Lymphatic Space Formation (NCIT:C35965), defined as the development of enlarged lymphatic
    channels, which fits the large channels but not the small ones or the malformed channels within
    the nodules. A search for "Vascular Channel" returned 12 terms, all in the branch; of the
    children of Vascular Channel Formation, Irregular Vascular Channel Formation (NCIT:C35973) fits
    only the malformed channels within the nodules and Slit-Like Vascular Channel Formation
    (NCIT:C49113) only the slit-like lumina, so the row takes the parent (27 Nov 2026).

- name: Vascular Endothelial Markers
  description: >-
    The endothelium of the nodules stains for the vascular endothelial markers CD31 and CD34 and for
    FLI1 in the 33-case series, and the endothelial cells for CD31, CD34 and ERG in the eight-case
    series, with smooth-muscle-actin-positive pericytes around the lumina. The abstract on three
    adult cases reports the spindle cells staining only focally for CD34 and CD31, and the cells
    lining the slit-like and sieve-like spaces not staining for von Willebrand factor.
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: CD31, CD34, FLI1 and ERG positive endothelium
    term:
      id: NCIT:C40998
      label: Immunophenotypic Finding
  notes: >-
    Bound to Immunophenotypic Finding, since the row covers four markers and NCIT's histopathology
    branch has a positive-finding term for only one of them: a label search for "CD34" returned 38
    terms, the one in the branch being CD34-Positive Neoplastic Cells Present (NCIT:C51144), and one
    for "CD34 Positive" returned NCIT:C148068, outside the branch. Searches for "CD31 Positive" and
    "FLI1 Positive" returned nothing, one for "CD31" a CD31 and a CD314 expression-measurement term,
    one for "FLI1" 12 terms, none in the branch, and one for "ERG" 788 terms, the only one in the
    branch being Divergent Differentiation (NCIT:C104333) (27 Nov 2026).

- name: Lymphatic Endothelial Markers
  description: >-
    Lymphatic markers are expressed too, though not in every compartment. The review lists
    podoplanin (D2-40), PROX1, LYVE-1 and VEGFR-3 in the lesional endothelium. A 314-tumour survey
    found a prominent PROX1-positive endothelial component in all 5 KHE it examined, with the
    spindle cells of the pericytic population PROX1-negative, and podoplanin in the 3 it examined
    further; the eight-case series' discussion places D2-40, LYVE-1 and VEGFR3, markers that series
    did not test itself, in the zones of lymphatic channels beside the glomeruloid areas; and in a
    thoracic series of 7 KHE and 6 kaposiform lymphangiomatosis patients every lesion examined had
    CD31- and D2-40-positive spindle cells. A study of 18 KHE among 75 vascular lesions found that
    tufted angioma shares KHE's endothelial immunophenotype, and found PROX1 helpful in
    distinguishing KHE from infantile haemangioma and pyogenic granuloma, which lacked it. PROX1 is
    not specific to KHE: the 314-tumour survey found it also in lymphangiomas, spindle cell and
    venous haemangiomas, retiform haemangioendothelioma and Kaposi sarcoma.
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: podoplanin (D2-40), PROX1, LYVE-1 and VEGFR-3 positive endothelium
    term:
      id: NCIT:C40998
      label: Immunophenotypic Finding
  notes: >-
    Bound to Immunophenotypic Finding. NCIT label searches for "Podoplanin", "D2-40" and "PROX1"
    returned the protein, gene and allele terms and a D2-40 staining method (NCIT:C178238); one for
    "LYVE" returned the LYVE1 gene and allele and four unrelated polyvesicular vitelline tumour and
    pattern terms; and ones for "VEGFR" and "FLT4" returned nothing in the histopathology branch.
    None is a finding about these markers (27 Nov 2026). The 75-lesion study's sentence on which
    markers each compartment carries is not cited: its abstract, as retrieved, lacks the plus and
    minus signs.

    juvenile haemangioma, and the review notes that the endothelium of infantile haemangioma is
    positive for GLUT1.

    Transporter" the glucose transporter proteins, and one for "Lewis" nothing in the histopathology
    branch; none is a finding about these markers (27 Nov 2026).

- name: Absent HHV-8
  description: >-
    Human herpesvirus 8 is absent: by immunostaining in 7 of 7 cases of an eight-case series, and by
    RT-PCR in all 3 cases tested in the 33-case series, which takes this to show a different
    pathogenesis from Kaposi sarcoma; the review lists the lesional endothelium as negative for
    HHV-8 staining, and the eight-case series' discussion restates, citing earlier work, that KHE is
    told from Kaposi sarcoma by its glomeruloid proliferations and the absence of HHV-8.

      label: Immunophenotypic Finding

    immunostaining. The only finding terms that searches for "HHV-8", "HHV8" and "Herpesvirus 8"
    returned are positive ones: Human Herpesvirus 8 Positive (NCIT:C146672), a laboratory result
    outside the histopathology branch, and Human Herpesvirus 8-Positive Neoplastic Cells Present

diagnosis:
- name: Magnetic resonance imaging
  description: >-
    Generally the first-line assessment, because the tumour's deep infiltration may not be apparent
    on examination or ultrasound. The lesion has ill-defined margins and crosses tissue planes,
    enhances diffusely, and is hypo- or iso-intense to muscle on T1 and hyperintense on T2.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: magnetic resonance imaging
    term:
      id: NCIT:C16809
      label: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is generally first-line assessment because the deep
      infiltrating nature of KHE may not be apparent on physical exam or on ultrasound.
    explanation: >-
      MRI is the first-line assessment.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      On MRI scans, KHEs usually exhibit ill-defined margins and are characterized by multiplanar
      involvement, diffuse enhancement, and adjacent fat stranding in unusual locations,
      iso-intensity relative to adjacent muscle on T1-weighted imaging, hyperintensity on
      T2-weighted imaging
    explanation: >-
      The appearance on MRI.

    explanation: >-

- name: Biopsy with immunohistochemistry
  description: >-
    Biopsy is the reference standard and shows the lymphatic-type endothelium, but it is often not
    possible or not advised in severe Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon. The diagnosis integrates the
    clinical, imaging, haematological and histological features, and even with all of them it can be
    unclear.

differential_diagnoses:
- name: Infantile Hemangioma
  description: >-
    One of the most important tumours to rule out. Infantile haemangioma grows dramatically at about
    5.5 to 7.5 weeks of age, its endothelial cells usually stain for GLUT1, which KHE lacks, and it
    lacks KHE's rounded nodules and the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon. KHE can be misdiagnosed as
    infantile haemangioma, as in a 19-month-old with a leg tumour that involved bone.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Usually GLUT1-positive; GLUT1 and Lewis Y antigen are its markers, absent from KHE nodules
  - No rounded nodules and no Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: infantile hemangioma
    term:
      id: MONDO:0011191
      label: capillary infantile hemangioma
  notes: >-
    MONDO has no class labelled infantile hemangioma: runoak -i sqlite:obo:mondo search "l~infantile
    hemangioma" returned capillary infantile hemangioma, infantile hemangioma of rare localization,
    isolated segmental infantile hemangioma and an obsolete hereditary class. The row
    binds MONDO:0011191 capillary infantile hemangioma, the class the Infantile_Hemangioma entry
    binds.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025

    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS

    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-
      The 2020 review names infantile haemangioma as one of the most important diseases to rule out.

      development into a disorganized mass of blood vessels
    explanation: >-
      Infantile haemangioma grows dramatically at 5.5 to 7.5 weeks of age.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-

    explanation: >-
      GLUT1 marks infantile haemangioma endothelium throughout its course and is absent in KHE.

    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:15105642
    reference_title: >-

- name: Congenital Hemangioma
  description: >-
    Arises in utero and is fully formed at birth, in rapidly involuting, partially involuting and
    non-involuting forms, and can look very like KHE in the newborn period. It does not grow
    progressively after birth, whereas KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon appears to grow and
    becomes engorged and purpuric. Mild consumption of clotting factors can occur, without bleeding,
    and tends to resolve within 1 to 2 weeks, but a rapidly involuting congenital haemangioma with
    profound, transient thrombocytopenia has been reported, and so have rapidly involuting ones with
    severe, life-threatening phenomenon. A 2014 report sets the rapidly involuting form apart from
    KHE and tufted angioma, which it names as associated with the phenomenon, while a 2023 case
    report puts it at under 10% of congenital haemangiomas against about 42% to 71% of KHE. On
    biopsy, both the rapidly involuting form and KHE are GLUT1-negative, but only KHE carries
    lymphatic markers.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Present and fully formed at birth, with no progressive growth after birth
  - Coagulopathy, when it occurs, usually mild and self-limited
  - Rapidly involuting form negative for lymphatic markers, which KHE expresses
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: congenital hemangioma
    term:
      id: MONDO:0018715
      label: congenital hemangioma
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Congenital hemangiomas are biologically and behaviorally distinct from KHEs. They are benign
      vascular tumors of infancy that arise in utero and are present and fully formed at birth. The
      3 variants of congenital hemangiomas are rapidly involuting congenital hemangiomas (RICHs),
      partially involuting congenital hemangiomas (PICHs) and noninvoluting congenital hemangiomas
      (NICHs)
    explanation: >-
      Congenital haemangiomas are distinct from KHE: benign, arising in utero, fully formed at
      birth, and in three forms.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Congenital hemangiomas can look very much like KHE particularly in the newborn period.
      Congenital hemangiomas do not exhibit progressive postnatal growth. In contrast, KHE tumors
      that develop KMP will appear to ‘grow’ and become engorged and purpuric in the first
      days/weeks/months of life.
    explanation: >-
      They can look like KHE in the newborn period, but do not grow progressively after birth,
      whereas KHE with the phenomenon appears to grow and becomes engorged and purpuric.
  - reference: PMID:32014025

    explanation: >-

- name: Tufted Angioma
  description: >-
    Occurs in the same young children, in the skin as red to purple plaques, and is, with KHE, one
    of the two tumours to which the 2020 review's definition of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon is
    limited. On ultrasound most tufted angiomas are well defined, and they are shallower and less
    vascular than KHE; on histology they show cannonball-like clusters of capillaries in the dermis.
    Some authors place the two at the benign and aggressive ends of one histological spectrum, and a
    2021 series says the WHO classification of soft-tissue tumours has combined them after a long
    debate.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Well-defined margins on ultrasound in most; KHE margins are ill defined
  - Shallower and less vascular than KHE on ultrasound
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: tufted angioma
    term:
      id: MONDO:0011927
      label: tufted angioma

    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

    reference_title: >-

- name: Kaposiform Lymphangiomatosis
  description: >-
    A rare, complex lymphatic disorder with multifocal or diffuse lesions that often involves the
    mediastinum, lungs, abdomen and several bones and, like KHE, contains spindled tumour cells. In
    a 2014 series most patients presented in childhood with respiratory or bleeding problems, and
    skin involvement was rare; in a 2019 series of thoracic disease, respiratory symptoms,
    effusions, thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy were common to both, presentation came later (mean
    26.7 against 4.1 months), and diffuse lung and extrathoracic lesions were seen only in
    kaposiform lymphangiomatosis. Its thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy overlap with
    the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: the 2014 series found the thrombocytopenia generally less
    severe, while a 2020 review notes that in some patients it is as severe. On histology its
    spindle cells form sparse, poorly marginated clusters rather than KHE's defined nodules; a
    somatic NRAS p.Q61R variant found in it is absent in KHE; and in the 2019 thoracic series it
    responded less to medical treatment.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Diffuse or multifocal disease that often involves the mediastinum, lungs, abdomen and bones
  - Later presentation, mostly in childhood; skin involvement rare
  - Spindle cells in sparse, poorly marginated clusters rather than defined nodules
  - Somatic NRAS p.Q61R, absent in KHE
  - More refractory to medical treatment
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
    term:
      id: MONDO:0018736
      label: kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      KLA is a rare, complex lymphatic disorder with multifocal or diffuse lesions. KLAs often
      involve the mediastinum, lung, abdomen and multiple bones
    explanation: >-
      The 2020 review: a rare, complex lymphatic disorder with multifocal or diffuse lesions that
      often involves the mediastinum, lungs, abdomen and several bones.
  - reference: PMID:24252784
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform lymphangiomatosis: a distinct aggressive lymphatic anomaly.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In contrast, most patients with KLA present in childhood with respiratory or bleeding
      concerns; cutaneous involvement is rare.
    explanation: >-
      In the 2014 series of 20, most patients presented in childhood with respiratory or bleeding
      problems, and skin involvement was rare, unlike KHE.
  - reference: PMID:31277673
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform lymphangiomatosis and kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: similarities and
      differences.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The mean ages at the time of the presentation of signs/symptoms were 26.7 months and 4.1
      months for KLA and KHE, respectively. Respiratory symptoms, pericardial and pleural effusion,
      thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy were common in both KLA and KHE. Diffuse lesions involving
      the lung and extrathoracic sites were observed in KLA but not in KHE.
    explanation: >-
      In 6 kaposiform lymphangiomatosis and 7 KHE involving the thorax: later presentation, symptoms
      and blood findings common to both, and diffuse lung and extrathoracic lesions only in
      kaposiform lymphangiomatosis.
  - reference: PMID:24252784
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform lymphangiomatosis: a distinct aggressive lymphatic anomaly.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT

    explanation: >-
      The 2014 series: the coagulopathy resembles the phenomenon, but the thrombocytopenia is

  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    reference_title: >-

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:31277673
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform lymphangiomatosis and kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: similarities and
      differences.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In KLA, the spindle cells were distributed in sparse and poorly marginated clusters, whereas

- name: Venous Malformation
  description: >-
    Extensive venous malformations are slow-flow malformations present at birth whose localized
    intravascular coagulopathy has been misdiagnosed as Kasabach-Merritt syndrome. It raises
    D-dimer, as the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon also does. The sources differ on fibrinogen: a 2002
    series of extensive limb disease and the 2020 review describe it as low, while a 2022 study
    found it reduced in 3 of 29 patients with venous malformations, two of them with signs of
    disseminated intravascular coagulation, and describes consumption of fibrinogen and platelets as
    what may follow when severe cases progress to it. Platelets are normal or only slightly
    decreased and no inflamed ecchymotic tumour is present; events such as sclerotherapy or surgery
    can convert the coagulopathy to disseminated intravascular coagulation. It comes from stasis in
    the malformed vessels rather than from platelet trapping in a tumour, is lifelong, and is
    treated differently.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Platelets normal or only slightly low at baseline; raised D-dimer is shared with the phenomenon
  - No large ecchymotic and inflammatory tumour
  - Enlarged, irregular venous channels lined by flattened endothelium
  notes: >-
    Left without a disease_term. A search of labels and synonyms in the local MONDO build,
    runoak -i sqlite:obo:mondo search "t~venous malformation", returned the HPO phenotype
    term HP:0012721 Venous malformation, which is not a disease class; specific forms (glomuvenous
    malformation, multiple cutaneous and mucosal venous malformations, primary intraosseous venous
    malformation, splenic venous malformation, dural sinus malformation); arteriovenous malformation
    classes, vein of Galen aneurysm and juvenile polyposis/hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
    syndrome; obsolete classes, among them obsolete rare venous malformation; and MONDO:0003083
    venous hemangioma. That class lists Venous malformation as an exact synonym, but MONDO defines
    it as a rare slow-growing benign tumour of aberrant and ectatic venous connections, files it
    under hemangioma and under congenital anomaly of cardiovascular system, cross-references it to
    ICD-O 9122/0 and NCIT:C4296, and places none of the venous malformation forms under it. Binding
    it would place a malformation under a tumour, so the row is left unbound.

- name: Infantile Fibrosarcoma
  description: >-
    A rare malignant soft-tissue tumour that mostly occurs before 1 year of age and can grow and
    become highly vascular within weeks or months; it is frequently misdiagnosed as infantile
    haemangioma or KHE. Bleeding or consumptive coagulopathy is rare with it. One case was first
    thought to be KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, and review of its laboratory studies
    suggested that disseminated intravascular coagulation may have been more likely. In a 2019 case,
    first treated as haemangioma until tissue examination gave the diagnosis, the infant developed
    disseminated intravascular coagulopathy with bleeding into the tumour during chemotherapy; its
    authors say the mechanism of the coagulopathy in this tumour is not well understood, and suggest
    that a process like Kasabach-Merritt syndrome could underlie it, given the tumour's vascularity.
  distinguishing_features:
  - Rare coagulopathy, possibly disseminated intravascular coagulation rather than the phenomenon
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: infantile fibrosarcoma

      id: MONDO:0004557
      label: congenital fibrosarcoma
  notes: >-

    local MONDO build.

- name: Kaposi Sarcoma
  description: >-
    KHE was set apart from infantile haemangioma in 1993 partly for its focal Kaposi-like
    appearance, and parts of the tumour resemble Kaposi sarcoma under the microscope. Human
    herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) stains positive in Kaposi sarcoma and has not been found in KHE:
    no transcripts in 3 tumours tested in a 2004 series, and negative immunostaining in 7 of 7 in a
    2021 series. The 2004 authors say the absence of HHV-8 underscores a pathogenesis different from
    Kaposi sarcoma.
  distinguishing_features:
  - HHV-8 positive in Kaposi sarcoma, not detected in KHE

treatments:
- name: Sirolimus
  description: >-
    An mTOR inhibitor. In a randomised trial in KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, in which
    sirolimus was given for at least 12 months, adding a short course of prednisolone raised the
    week-4 platelet response from 24 of 36 to 35 of 37; in a randomised trial in KHE without the
    phenomenon, low-dose sirolimus was non-inferior to high-dose at one year (about 90% response in
    both); in a cohort of 167 patients, 92.2% had a durable response.
    On dose, a series of 21 patients, started on sirolimus alone at 0.8 mg/m2 twice a day once there
    was no sign of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon aiming for a trough of 5 to 20 ng/mL, found
    faster tumour shrinkage above a trough of 10 ng/mL and no further gain above 15, in groups of 8,
    7 and 6 patients; the randomised trial in KHE without the phenomenon found a trough of 5 to 8
    ng/mL non-inferior to 10 to 15 for a volume reduction of at least 20% at month 12, with similar
    total and serious adverse events but fewer respiratory, skin and mucosal ones. In a
    pharmacokinetic model of 17 children aged 0.2 to 6 years, the drug's apparent clearance rose
    with age and was higher in boys than in girls of the same age, which the authors put down to
    body weight. In the patients with the phenomenon in a 52-patient series, tumour shrinkage did
    not differ significantly between the 21 given short-term prednisolone for severe symptoms and
    those on sirolimus alone, whereas the randomised prednisolone trial in KHE with the phenomenon
    reported better objective lesion responses at month 12 with it. On stopping, rebound growth
    followed discontinuation in 17.3% of the patients of the cohort of 167 who stopped sirolimus
    (the abstract does not say how many stopped), associated with early discontinuation and with
    mixed lesion type, for which the abstract's own confidence interval includes 1; in a series of
    26, 25 of them with the phenomenon, 20 completed a course of 28.3 months on average, and the
    series had no recurrence over a median follow-up of 32 months (the abstract does not say whether
    follow-up ran from the start or the end of treatment). In the cohort of 167, nonresponse,
    relapse and long-term sequelae remained despite intensified and prolonged treatment. On harms,
    serious adverse events were most common in the first year and long-term treatment brought no
    unacceptable cumulative toxicity in that cohort; in the randomised prednisolone trial, total and
    grade 3-4 adverse events were similar with and without prednisolone; no patient in the
    52-patient series stopped permanently for toxicity, and the 26-patient series reported mild side
    effects; and a 4-month-old on sirolimus and a prednisolone taper developed Pneumocystis
    pneumonia with respiratory failure needing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, after which the
    authors advise considering prophylaxis.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  dosing_interval: twice a day
  dosing_interval_days: 0.5
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: sirolimus
      term:
        id: CHEBI:9168
        label: sirolimus

  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Lymphatic-Type Endothelial Proliferation
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Aimed at the growth of the tumour's endothelium.
      How sirolimus acts in KHE is not settled. A 2025 review lists possible effects on platelet
      activation, inflammation, angiogenesis, lymphangiogenesis and fibrosis, of which the
      antiangiogenic and antilymphangiogenic effects bear on this node, and the 2020 review places
      it beside antilymphatic strategies. Serum angiopoietin-2 fell after 12 months of treatment in
      kaposiform lymphangiomatosis and in KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, reported
      together in the abstract, with most patients responding, which may track the phenomenon rather
      than the endothelium; and sirolimus downregulated ATG9B in endothelial cells cultured from
      patients' tumours, a preliminary transcriptome finding.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:38903724
      reference_title: >-
        Treatment experience for different risk groups of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: >-
        Rapamycin works by inhibiting the expression of various cytokines, including VEGF, and by
        blocking mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signal pathways, which induces anti-vascular
        proliferation and promotes apoptosis
      explanation: >-
        How sirolimus acts, as the cohort's discussion states it: mTOR blockade against vascular
        proliferation. INDIRECT: not shown in this tumour.
    - reference: PMID:39369447
      reference_title: >-
        Sirolimus for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Potential mechanisms of action and
        resistance.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: >-
        The prevention of platelet activation and inflammation, along with antiangiogenic effects,
        the inhibition of lymphangiogenesis, the attenuation of fibrosis, or a combination of all
        these effects, may be responsible for the therapeutic effects of sirolimus.
      explanation: >-

- name: Corticosteroids
  description: >-
    Recommended as a first-line treatment of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon because they raise the
    platelet count quickly; given alone, many cases do not improve, with response rates of 10 to
    27%. The 2020 review gives oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg a day or intravenous methylprednisolone 1.6
    mg/kg a day, and recommends them for the severe Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon together with
    vincristine or sirolimus. One cohort's discussion describes starting methylprednisolone at 2 to
    3 mg/kg a day for less than a week, and says 5 to 6 mg/kg a day can be used for extremely low
    platelet counts and life-threatening conditions; its results report giving every child with the
    phenomenon who was operated on high-dose methylprednisolone (5 to 6 mg/kg a day), a haemostatic
    or immunoglobulin before surgery, and its abstract says 89% of those operated on had high-dose
    methylprednisolone beforehand. Prednisolone is also the add-on in the randomised trial of
    sirolimus. The review notes that the 2013 consensus recommendations of corticosteroids,
    vincristine or both rest on expert opinion rather than rigorous clinical studies. Long-term use
    brings temporary growth retardation, a higher risk of infection and behavioural change, and the
    21-child series, citing earlier work, adds hypertension, sleep disturbance and hyperglycaemia;
    so the review advises weaning them as soon as medically feasible, and the VASCERN-VASCA pathway
    tapering and stopping them once the phenomenon has resolved and the child is stable.

- name: Vincristine
  description: >-
    A vinca alkaloid, given intravenously at 0.05 mg/kg once a week in the 2020 review's table,
    through a central line. Consensus-derived guidelines recommended vincristine, with or without
    corticosteroids, as first-line treatment of KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, and the
    review notes that the 2013 consensus recommendations of corticosteroids, vincristine or both
    rest on expert opinion rather than rigorous clinical studies; the review now considers sirolimus
    with corticosteroids a first-line therapy (versus vincristine with corticosteroids); many
    clinicians and families prefer sirolimus because vincristine needs a central line; and a
    21-child series says sirolimus has superseded it in many centres. The VASCERN-VASCA pathway adds
    vincristine when a lesion compresses vital structures or lies in a life-threatening site, or
    when sirolimus and corticosteroids fail; notes that, once the diagnosis has been re-confirmed,
    adding it can shrink a tumour without the phenomenon that has not responded; and allows stopping
    it once the lesion no longer shrinks. First-line vincristine has an overall response rate of
    72%; in a multicentre cohort that pools KHE with tufted angioma, its radiological response at
    three months was higher than sirolimus's, with no difference at six. In the single-centre series
    of 21 children, 16 were treated with vincristine, weekly for 6 to 12 weeks and then less often,
    for a median total of 185 days: 11 needed no other treatment, 3 moved on to sirolimus, and there
    were no recurrences over a median follow-up of 6.1 years; the series acknowledges an
    institutional preference for vincristine. The review cites mounting evidence that vincristine
    alone fails in very severe disease, while in that series the 3 children with the severe
    Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon who began vincristine had the phenomenon resolve after two doses,
    alongside supportive measures; one of them later moved to sirolimus. Complications there were
    common but, in the authors' words, mild in most: 15 of 16 had at least one, 13 were admitted
    with a febrile illness, 8 had what the authors call bone marrow suppression (a haemoglobin below
    100 g/L, managed with iron), 6 had poor weight gain or growth, one of them admitted for tube
    feeding, 3 central lines were removed early, and 2 children had possible neuropathy, a transient
    ptosis. Another cohort, citing earlier work, says vincristine is given to children with the
    phenomenon who do not respond to corticosteroids, but is not used routinely because of its
    complications, among them myelosuppression in neonates, peripheral neuropathy, constipation and
    intestinal obstruction.

- name: Surgical resection
  description: >-
    Complete resection is an option where it can be done safely, but surgery is rarely an option for
    extensive tumours or where it would badly impair function. The VASCERN-VASCA pathway says
    radical surgery that avoids functional defects and mutilation can be curative for the rare small
    tumour without the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, and after failed medical treatment reserves
    surgery for the rare tumours that can be removed completely without mutilation. Elective
    resection during the active phenomenon is ill advised: these young children, with very vascular
    tumours, are at higher risk of blood loss, iatrogenic injury and a worse coagulopathy. The
    review also cites evidence that manipulating the tumour, by surgery or trauma, can set off the
    phenomenon, whether or not the child has had it before. Surgery can also remove a fibrofatty
    residuum or reconstruct damaged structures. Both cited series nonetheless operated on children
    with the phenomenon. In one single-centre cohort, where over 90% were operated on, the authors
    favoured early surgery; all 8 low-risk patients recovered after surgery without recurrence, and
    6 cases (9%) recurred after a few months as small lesions. In a single-centre series of 21
    children, 6 tumours were excised, and the phenomenon resolved within 24 hours of the operation
    in the 2 of them with the severe Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: tumour resection
    term:
      id: NCIT:C164212
      label: Tumor Resection
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Conversely, surgery can be an approach for tumors in which a complete and safe resection can
      be performed
    explanation: >-
      Surgery is an option where complete, safe resection is possible.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Elective resection of a KHE during the active phase of KMP is unusually not necessary and is
      ill advised.
    explanation: >-
      Elective resection during the active phenomenon is ill advised.

    supports: SUPPORT

    snippet: >-
      Early surgical intervention may be the most definitive treatment option for most patients with
      KHE; multimodality treatment is the best choice for the extremely high-risk group.
    explanation: >-
      The cohort's authors favour early surgery, from a series in which most children were operated
      on.

    reference_title: >-

    explanation: >-
      Surgery is rarely an option for extensive tumours or where it would badly impair function.

- name: Antiplatelet agents
  description: >-
    Ticlopidine and aspirin, which inhibit platelet aggregation, have been used in
    the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: ticlopidine with aspirin, and ticlopidine with vincristine. The
    2020 review gives ticlopidine by mouth at 10 mg/kg a day, recommends vincristine with aspirin,
    ticlopidine or both for the severe Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, and advises against ticlopidine
    alone in the phenomenon; the VASCERN-VASCA pathway notes that some centres use them despite a
    lack of evidence in the literature, and although platelet function is already impaired in the
    phenomenon. The phenomenon's own treatment is curated in the Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome entry.
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy

    - preferred_term: aspirin

  description: >-
    Interferon alfa was among the older drug treatments of KHE, but responses to it are variable and
    unpredictable, and its side effects are significant, spastic diplegia among them; the 2020
    review advises against it in children under one year old because of its neurological toxicity.

    modality is OTHER: PROTEIN_REPLACEMENT names the replacement of a missing protein, which this is
    not, and no value names a cytokine. The review's table gives a subcutaneous dose whose power of
    ten is lost in the text as retrieved, so the dose is not quoted.

- name: Transarterial embolisation
  description: >-
    Arterial embolisation can at first reduce blood flow from the tumour and the risk of high-output
    cardiac failure, and may have a role in controlling the disease in children with the
    Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon. It is technically difficult, since the feeding vessels in these
    young children are very small, and as an invasive procedure it may worsen the blood counts. The
    VASCERN-VASCA pathway keeps it, with surgery, for when medical treatment fails, recommends that
    referral centres do it, notes that in selected cases combining it with medical treatment can
    stabilise the child, and that embolising before surgery may shrink the tumour for a time and
    reduce bleeding at operation.
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: transarterial embolisation
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15917
      label: Arterial Embolization

progression:
- phase: Onset
  description: >-
    Mostly in infancy: onset in infancy in 93% of 107 patients in one series, and as newborns in
    60%.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22871490
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: atypical features and risks of Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon in
      107 referrals.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      KHE manifested in infancy in 93% of cases, with 60% as neonates.
    explanation: >-
      Onset in infancy in 93% of 107.
- phase: Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon
  description: >-
    Usually early. In a series of 146 patients, which defined the phenomenon as a platelet count
    below 100 × 10^9/L, it developed in 102 (69.9%), from the first day of life to 60 months of age
    (median 1 month). It was present at birth in 39.2% of those 102 and began within the first 6
    months of age in 91.2%, after 1 year of age in four; 48.0% had no sign of it when the lesion was
    first assessed and developed it a median 1.25 months later, and in four, all with deep lesions,
    it was noted before a tumour mass was identified. In 107 referrals, 71% developed it, 11% after
    initial presentation. In 70 children in a 2024 series, which defined it from platelet counts and
    coagulation indices, 78% did, with thrombocytopenia starting at a median of 27.8 days of age,
    though that series' own counts by depth stage add up to 48 of the 70. The 107-referral series
    (2013) gives no definition in its abstract, so the three rates are not strictly comparable.
    Which tumours develop it: in the 146-patient series, a younger age at which the lesion was
    discovered, its size and a mixed lesion (a cutaneous lesion with deep infiltration into muscle,
    bone, intrathoracic or retroperitoneal sites) remained associated with it after adjustment (odds
    ratios 11.9, 5.08 and 2.96), while a trunk site was associated only before adjustment (87%
    against 59% at other sites, odds ratio 4.70), and head-neck and extremity lesions less often had
    it. Before adjustment, lesions discovered before 6 months of age had higher odds than those
    discovered at 12 months or later (odds ratio 59, 95% confidence interval 7.38 to 472; 1 of the
    15 discovered at 12 months or later had it); lesions of 5 to 8 cm and of 8 cm or more had odds
    ratios of 6.8 and 14.2 against those under 5 cm (the phenomenon in 71% and 83%, against 26%
    under 5 cm); and mixed lesions had about four times the odds of the phenomenon that superficial
    ones had (80% against 50%). Deep, noncutaneous lesions as a group were not a significant factor
    (10 of 18 had it). By site, every lesion involving the mediastinum or the peritoneal cavity had
    it (three of the deep lesions were in the peritoneal cavity; the number involving the
    mediastinum is not given), as did 7 of 9 with retroperitoneal involvement (the authors, citing
    an earlier report, suggest that small retroperitoneal lesions without the phenomenon might go
    undetected), while none of the six confined to bone, joint and muscle did. The authors suggest
    those six may be physically constrained from expansion, and note that they tended to be more
    focal and smaller than mixed lesions. In the 107 referrals, a tumour infiltrating muscle or
    deeper was "6.3-fold more likely" to show it, and a retroperitoneal or intrathoracic site
    "18-fold higher", against a superficial tumour (the abstract does not say whether these are odds
    ratios); retroperitoneal and intrathoracic tumours had it in 85% and 100%; and tumours limited
    to bone or presenting after infancy did not. A 2020 review, which shares authors with the
    146-patient series, puts the risk highest for congenital tumours of large size, especially over
    8 cm. Among its limitations the 146-patient series names its retrospective design, the treatment
    of several congenital lesions that had no sign of the phenomenon at referral and might otherwise
    have developed it, and possible referral bias. The phenomenon itself is curated separately as
    Kasabach-Merritt Syndrome.

      Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The limitations of this study include its retrospective approach. Multiple neonates and young
      infants with congenital lesions did not experience KMP when referred to our departments, and
      several of these congenital lesions were treated. Perhaps these lesions would have grown
      faster and developed KMP if they had not been treated.
    explanation: >-
      The series' limitations: its retrospective design, and congenital lesions without the
      phenomenon at referral that were treated and might otherwise have developed it.
  - reference: PMID:29603128
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform haemangioendothelioma: clinical features, complications and risk factors for
      Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      the high rate of complications in our cases might reflect a referral bias because many
      patients who were enrolled in our study were likely to be at higher risk.
    explanation: >-
      A further limitation: its high complication rate may reflect referral of higher-risk patients.
- phase: Outcome
  description: >-
    The tumour can persist: about 17.4% of 167 patients on long-term sirolimus still had active
    disease or changed body structures at last follow-up, and in a cohort of 70 children all five
    treated without surgery (medicines, with or without sclerotherapy) were alive with tumour.
    Untreated tumour becomes progressively fibrotic, and some patients develop contractures and
    chronic pain; quality of life is lower than in healthy children. Deaths are few in recent
    cohorts: 2 of 70 in one, 2 of 159 (KHE and tufted angioma together) in another.
    Citing earlier studies, the 2018 musculoskeletal cohort states that in most patients the lesion
    is still present after long-term treatment and that residual lesions become progressively
    fibrotic; in that cohort, decreased joint motion appeared in one patient after sirolimus was
    tapered and stopped at 18 months, and improved on further courses.
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1002/ijc.34509
    reference_title: >-
      Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing
      successes and ongoing challenges
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At the last follow‐up, approximately 17.4% of patients had active disease and/or changes in
      body structures to a variable extent.
    explanation: >-
      Active disease or changed body structures in about 17.4% at last follow-up.
  - reference: PMID:38903724
    reference_title: >-
      Treatment experience for different risk groups of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Of these 70 cases, 5 underwent medical treatment with or without sclerotherapy; all of them
      were alive with tumors, and 2 cases were still taking sirolimus by the end of follow-up.
    explanation: >-
      Residual tumour in all five treated without surgery.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The diffuse intraarticular and periarticular fibrosis can further aggravate muscular atrophy
      and lead to subluxations and flexion contracture of the involved joints. Patients may
      eventually suffer from recalcitrant pain and fixed contractures
    explanation: >-
      Fibrosis can lead to contractures and chronic pain.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Pathologically, untreated KHE lesions are characterized by progressive fibrosis
    explanation: >-
      Untreated lesions become progressively fibrotic.
  - reference: PMID:35281237
    reference_title: >-
      Health-Related Quality of Life in Children With Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The scores of physiological and psychosocial domains in all age groups of patients with KHE
      were lower than those of normal children (P < 0.01).
    explanation: >-
      Lower quality of life than in healthy children, in 91 children.
  - reference: PMID:38903724
    reference_title: >-
      Treatment experience for different risk groups of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Two KMP cases died at 1 and 3 months after discharge, but the immediate causes of death were
      unknown.
    explanation: >-
      Two deaths among 70, causes unknown.
  - reference: DOI:10.1002/pbc.30779
    reference_title: >-
      Treatment practices and response in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A multicenter cohort
      study
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Of 159 unique KHE/TA subjects, Kasabach–Merritt phenomenon (KMP) was present in 64 (40.3%),
      and only two patients were deceased (1.3%).
    explanation: >-
      Two deaths among 159. INDIRECT: KHE and tufted angioma are pooled.
  - reference: PMID:30233248
    reference_title: >-
      Musculoskeletal complication in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
      without Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: clinical characteristics and management.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In most patients, the lesion was still present even after long-term treatment.
    explanation: >-
      The cohort's discussion, citing earlier work: residual tumour after long-term treatment in
      most patients.
  - reference: PMID:30233248
    reference_title: >-
      Musculoskeletal complication in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
      without Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: clinical characteristics and management.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:30233248
    reference_title: >-
      Musculoskeletal complication in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
      without Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon: clinical characteristics and management.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      One patient who was tapered and discontinued from sirolimus after 18 months of treatment

    explanation: >-

      improved on further courses.

genetic:
- name: GNA14
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GNA14
    term:
      id: hgnc:4382
      label: GNA14
  relationship_type: DISPUTED
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  notes: >-
    A somatic activating c.614A>T (p.Gln205Leu) variant, reported in one KHE in the 2016 discovery
    study (the 2020 review's 1/3 of KHE specimens); a later sequencing series of five KHEs and two
    tufted angiomas found none, and the cause of most tumours is unknown. Recorded as DISPUTED
    because no cited study has found it in a further KHE, and the review says it is not known
    whether the GNAQ-family changes found in KHE are causes or arise later in the tumour.
    Kasabach-Merritt_Syndrome records the same gene as a somatic driver.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27476652
    reference_title: >-
      GNA14 Somatic Mutation Causes Congenital and Sporadic Vascular Tumors by MAPK Activation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We found somatic activating GNA14 c.614A>T (p.Gln205Leu) mutations in one KHE, one TA, and one
      LCH and a GNA11 c.547C>T (p.Arg183Cys) mutation in two LCH lesions.
    explanation: >-
      The original report of the variant in KHE.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Remarkably, the somatic activating GNA14 c.614A > T (p.Gln205Leu) mutation was found in 1/3 of
      KHE specimens and in 1/4 of TA specimens, although these studies were weakened by small sample
      size
    explanation: >-
      The review's figure for the same finding, 1/3 of KHE specimens.
  - reference: PMID:31423605
    reference_title: >-
      Tufted angioma with associated Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon caused by somatic mutation in
      GNA14.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here, we explored the genetic mechanism underlying a case of TA associated with KMP via
      targeted sequencing of laser capture micro-dissected lesion and blood DNA, and identified a
      somatic, activating GNA14 mutation specific to the tumor.
    explanation: >-
      In a tufted angioma, a somatic activating GNA14 variant was in the lesion and not in blood.
      INDIRECT: the related tumour, one case.
  - reference: PMID:31887709
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma and tufted angioma - (epi)genetic analysis including
      genome-wide methylation profiling.
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Using next generation sequencing, heterogeneous mutations were found in a subset of cases
      (2/7) without the presence of GNA14 mutations, previously reported in KHE and TA.
    explanation: >-
      A sequencing series of five KHEs and two tufted angiomas in which no GNA14 mutation was found.
  - reference: PMID:32014025
    reference_title: >-
      Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      However, it is important to note that although GNAQ mutations have been found in KHE, we do
      not know whether they are causative or develop secondarily in the tumor.
    explanation: >-
      The review states that GNAQ mutations (in its words) have been found in KHE, restating the
      2016 study, and that it is not known whether they cause the tumour or arise later in it.

notes: >-
  Cut around Kasabach-Merritt_Syndrome, which holds the platelet-trapping mechanism and its
  treatment; this entry holds the tumour and its own trial records, five of them also rows on that
  entry, and its platelet step only hands over to that entry. Repetition between the two is
  deliberate where a fact belongs to both. The
  share of patients with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon differs widely between series (42% to 78%
  in the KHE series cited here), so each figure names its cohort.
discussions:
- discussion_id: khe_tufted_angioma_one_spectrum_or_two
  prompt: >-
    Are kaposiform haemangioendothelioma and tufted angioma one neoplasm at two ends of a spectrum,
    or two related diseases?
  kind: CONTROVERSY
  status: OPEN
  attaches_to:
  - mechanistic_hypotheses#tufted_angioma_one_spectrum
  - mechanistic_hypotheses#tufted_angioma_two_diseases
  rationale: >-
    The 2020 review treats the two as one spectrum, a methylation study reads them as potentially
    one entity, and four of five comparative studies from 2019 to 2022 (which may include some of
    these), counted by a 2022 review of the literature, considered them one spectrum; a 2003 report
    described one patient's tumour changing between them, a 2023 letter described tufted angioma
    appearing where a KHE had been, and the WHO classification, as two cited series describe it,
    suggests they may be manifestations or stages of one tumour, or has combined them. The same 2003
    report notes that the classification then in use kept them as separate entities, one study in
    the 2022 review treats them as different, and the sources describe differences in location,
    behaviour, histology and imaging that fit either reading. MONDO keeps separate classes, and this
    entry maps tufted angioma as a related match rather than a subtype. Which reading holds bears on
    whether findings, risks and treatment results reported for one tumour, or for series that pool
    both, can be carried over to the other.

Create: Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma · 2026-11-21T00:55:36Z · View source

New entry for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (MONDO:0016236), a rare, locally aggressive vascular tumour of infancy and early childhood. Curated by hand from cached sources: a 2020 review (full text), a 2024 single-centre cohort of 70 children (full text), a 2023 platelet-function study (full text), the 2013 Boston series of 107 patients, a 2021 MRI series of 64, the 2016 GNA14 discovery study, a 2019 tufted angioma case, a 2020 sequencing and methylation series, the 2022 randomised trial of sirolimus with and without prednisolone, a 2025 randomised non-inferiority trial of low- against high-dose sirolimus, a 2023 long-term sirolimus cohort of 167, a 2024 multicentre cohort of 159 that pools KHE with tufted angioma, a 2020 chronic lymphoedema cohort of 118, a 2022 quality-of-life study and a 2025 consensus statement. The entry is cut around Kasabach-Merritt_Syndrome, which keeps the platelet-trapping mechanism, its treatment and the trial records; here the platelet step only hands over to that entry, and every sentence quoted in both entries carries the same evidence_source in both. The chain runs from a GNA14 node for tumours carrying a somatic activating variant (one KHE in the cited studies; it is not marked as the cancer-origin node, because the variant's causal role is open, and its causal edge belongs to an emerging mechanistic hypothesis; no cell is bound, because the cited sources do not establish in which cell the variant arises; the node binds G protein-coupled receptor binding, which the review states for the GNAQ family) through lymphatic-type endothelial proliferation and local infiltration to the mass, pain, joint involvement, bone destruction, chronic lymphoedema and the platelet step. GNA14 is recorded as DISPUTED: one KHE in the discovery study, none in a later series of five, and the review calls causation unknown; Kasabach-Merritt_Syndrome records it as a somatic driver. Seven phenotype rows name the cohort behind each frequency, because the series disagree, notably on how often the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon occurs (42% to 78% in the KHE series cited). Diagnosis rows cover MRI and biopsy with immunohistochemistry; treatment rows cover sirolimus (two randomised trials, of sirolimus with and without prednisolone and of low- against high-dose sirolimus), corticosteroids, vincristine and surgery, each linked to a node: sirolimus, vincristine and surgery to the tumour nodes they act on, corticosteroids to the platelet trapping they are given for. Onset and outcome phases, an incidence row and a prevalence row complete it. The deep-research report generated for this entry was used as a lead and is not committed. Validated with just validate and count-verified-snippets (102 of 102).
